fact_check.fact: 12 modifiable risk factors account for around 40% of worldwide dementias
fact_check.note: Confirmed against the Lancet 2020 Executive Summary and Figure 7 Population Attributable Fraction (PAF) calculations.

fact_check.fact: Air pollution Population Attributable Fraction (PAF) is 2.3%
fact_check.note: Confirmed against Table 1 and the pollution section. The authors note this relies on a single Canadian cohort with low baseline pollution, meaning the global PAF is likely conservative/underestimated.

fact_check.fact: SPRINT MIND trial significantly reduced probable dementia incidence
fact_check.note: The Lancet text explicitly states intensive blood pressure treatment significantly reduced mild cognitive impairment (HR 0.8), but the reduction in probable dementia was not statistically significant (HR 0.8, 95% CI 0.7-1.0).

research_page.title: 2020 Lancet Commission on dementia prevention, intervention, and care
research_page.description: The 2020 Lancet Commission identifies 12 modifiable risk factors that account for 40% of worldwide dementias and provides life-course recommendations.
research_page.authors_line_md: GL et al. — University College London (UCL)
research_page.takeaway_md: The 2020 Lancet Commission model estimates that 40% of global dementia cases are linked to 12 modifiable risk factors. While these epidemiological associations are robust, clinical trials of lifestyle interventions show more modest effects, suggesting prevention requires broad public health policy alongside individual behavioral changes.
key_findings_md: Modifying 12 risk factors across the life-course could theoretically prevent or delay up to 40% of global dementia cases (Lancet 2020, Executive Summary).

Three newly added factors (excessive alcohol consumption, traumatic brain injury, and air pollution) join nine established factors to form the updated life-course model (Lancet 2020, Executive Summary).
Excessive midlife alcohol consumption (>21 units/week) is associated with a 1.18 relative risk of developing dementia (Lancet 2020, Table 1).
Traumatic brain injury of any severity increases all-cause dementia risk, with a pooled relative risk of 1.84 (Lancet 2020, Figure 6).

Amyloid and tau biomarkers indicate elevated disease risk but do not reliably predict symptomatic progression in cognitively normal individuals over clinically relevant timeframes (Lancet 2020, Biomarkers section).
research_page.methods_md: Systematic review, meta-analysis, and epidemiological modeling. The authors synthesized global observational cohort and clinical trial data across a life-course duration to estimate Population Attributable Fractions (PAF) for 12 modifiable risk factors.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: Epidemiological models suggest high preventability, but interventional trials show mixed results. The [FINGER trial](/trials/finger-nct01041989) demonstrated modest cognitive test score improvements from a multidomain lifestyle intervention, while the [MAPT trial](/trials/mapt-nct00672685) found no significant slowing of decline in frail older adults. Pharmacological risk modification in SPRINT MIND successfully reduced mild cognitive impairment, but randomized trials struggle to achieve the large dementia incidence reductions predicted by theoretical population models.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public and media reception has been highly positive, focusing on the empowering message that 40% of dementia risk is modifiable. However, caregiver communities express mixed feelings, noting that the emphasis on "prevention" can inadvertently generate guilt or victim-blaming for patients who developed the disease despite maintaining healthy lifestyles. Scientific reception praises the life-course model but cautions against conflating population-level associations with individual clinical guarantees.
caveats_md: The epidemiological model relies on observational cohort data which assumes strict causality between risk factors and dementia onset, leaving the possibility that factors like late-life depression or social withdrawal are actually early symptoms of the disease rather than root causes.
The global preventability estimates lean heavily on data from high-income countries, likely misrepresenting or underestimating the true risk factor burden in low- and middle-income countries.

Because no single dataset tracks all 12 risk factors simultaneously, the statistical modeling relies on overlapping cohorts and imputations, meaning the exact combined impact of multiple overlapping risks remains theoretical.
relates_to_md: [Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — Evaluates the clinical utility and predictive limits of amyloid and tau testing in asymptomatic populations.
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Notes the failure of secondary prevention trials targeting amyloid alone in asymptomatic individuals.

[Next Steps After an Alzheimer's Diagnosis](/journey/newly-diagnosed) — Emphasizes the importance of holistic post-diagnostic care and avoiding harmful psychotropic medications for neuropsychiatric symptoms.

trial_pages.title: FINGER
trial_pages.description: Multidomain lifestyle counseling intervention for adults 60-77 years with an increased dementia risk score.
trial_pages.sponsor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare
trial_pages.population: Adults 60-77 years with increased dementia risk score
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Cognitive impairment assessed with a Neuropsychological Test Battery
trial_pages.why_md: FINGER is a landmark multidomain lifestyle intervention trial designed to assess whether diet, exercise, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring can prevent cognitive decline. It serves as a primary piece of interventional evidence evaluated by public health models for mitigating [modifiable risk factors](/research/papers/lancet-commission-2020-dementia-prevention).
status_log_md: **2015-06** — 2-year multidomain intervention results demonstrate modest but significant improvement in cognitive test scores ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25771249/)).
trial_pages.results_md: The 2-year multidomain lifestyle intervention significantly improved overall cognitive performance (measured by NTB z-score) compared to standard counseling. Extended follow-up for hard dementia incidence is ongoing.

trial_pages.title: MAPT
trial_pages.description: Omega-3 and/or multidomain lifestyle intervention in frail elderly subjects aged 70 years and older.
trial_pages.population: Frail elderly subjects aged 70 years and older
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change in cognitive function at 36 months (composite score)
trial_pages.why_md: The MAPT trial evaluated whether omega-3 supplementation, alone or combined with a multidomain lifestyle intervention, could slow cognitive decline in frail older adults. It provides crucial context on the limitations and challenges of translating epidemiological [risk models](/research/papers/lancet-commission-2020-dementia-prevention) into successful clinical interventions.
status_log_md: **2017-05** — 3-year randomized trial results show a lack of significant effect of the multidomain intervention on cognitive function in frail elderly adults ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28359749/)).
trial_pages.results_md: The multidomain intervention (with or without omega-3 fatty acids) failed to significantly slow cognitive decline over 3 years compared to placebo in frail older adults.

timeline_entries.title: 2015-06 — FINGER trial demonstrates benefits of multidomain lifestyle intervention
timeline_entries.body_md: The [FINGER trial](/trials/finger-nct01041989) reads out 2-year results showing modest cognitive performance improvements, providing interventional support for multidomain lifestyle modifications.

timeline_entries.title: 2019-02 — SPRINT MIND shows intensive blood pressure control reduces MCI
timeline_entries.body_md: The SPRINT MIND trial demonstrates that intensive antihypertensive therapy reduces the incidence of mild cognitive impairment, validating vascular health as a key target for [dementia prevention](/research/papers/lancet-commission-2020-dementia-prevention).

timeline_entries.title: 2020-07 — Lancet Commission updates modifiable risk factor model
timeline_entries.body_md: The Lancet Commission publishes an updated life-course model adding air pollution, traumatic brain injury, and excessive alcohol, estimating 40% of dementias are tied to 12 [modifiable risk factors](/research/papers/lancet-commission-2020-dementia-prevention).
